elements.quote: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of English-language literature published from January 2015 to June 2025
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review and meta-analysis.

elements.quote: We updated the evidence on post-ERCP adverse events in children, pooled post-ERCP pancreatitis (PEP) incidence when study-level data allowed, and summarized reported risk factors and prevention strategies.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective of the review explicitly.

elements.quote: Eligible quantitative analyses included non-overlapping pediatric primary studies reporting extractable numerators and denominators for post-ERCP adverse events.
elements.reason: Main inclusion criteria (population, study type, language, dates) are given, but exclusion criteria are not explicitly stated in the abstract.

elements.quote: of English-language literature published from January 2015 to June 2025 in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library
elements.reason: Information sources are identified, but the January 2015 to June 2025 range refers to publication dates of included literature, not an explicit statement of when each source was last searched.
The abstract does not mention any risk-of-bias assessment methods; these appear only in the Methods section (text_8).

elements.quote: Random-effects meta-analysis of proportions was planned for outcomes with at least three eligible studies. Risk-factor and prevention data were summarized narratively when definitions or adjustment strategies were too heterogeneous for pooling.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the methods used to synthesize and present results.

elements.quote: Sixty-five sources were included in the qualitative synthesis, and 15 non-overlapping primary studies contributed extractable PEP numerators and denominators for quantitative synthesis.
elements.reason: Numbers of included studies/sources are reported, but the total number of participants is not stated and study characteristics are only minimally summarized.

elements.quote: PEP was the most frequent adverse event, with a pooled incidence of approximately 7.3% (95% CI, 5.1% to 10.4%; I-squared = 83.7%). ... Bleeding was uncommon and perforation was rare but clinically important.
elements.reason: The abstract reports results for the main outcomes (PEP, bleeding, perforation) with study counts for the quantitative synthesis.

elements.quote: a pooled incidence of approximately 7.3% (95% CI, 5.1% to 10.4%; I-squared = 83.7%)
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports the summary estimate with its 95% confidence interval.

elements.quote: Risk-factor and prevention data were summarized narratively when definitions or adjustment strategies were too heterogeneous for pooling.
elements.reason: No head-to-head group comparison is made in the review; risk factors were summarized narratively without comparative effect estimates, so direction-of-effect reporting does not apply.

elements.quote: The pooled estimate provides a current benchmark, but heterogeneity and inconsistent reporting limit certainty.
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes key limitations of the evidence (heterogeneity, inconsistent reporting).

elements.quote: Pediatric ERCP carries measurable adverse-event risk, particularly PEP. ... Standardized pediatric definitions, non-overlapping reporting, and prospective multicenter datasets are needed.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications.
The abstract does not state the funding source; funding appears only in the back matter (text_22).

elements.quote: Registration: PROSPERO CRD420251084264.
elements.reason: The abstract provides both the register name (PROSPERO) and the registration number.

elements.quote: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is increasingly used in children with pancreatobiliary disease, but pediatric adverse-event estimates remain variable.
elements.reason: The abstract background briefly states the current state of knowledge (increasing pediatric ERCP use) and an uncertainty (variable adverse-event estimates), but the retrieved evidence does not include a full Introduction section elaborating existing knowledge and uncertainties in detail.

elements.quote: We updated the evidence on post-ERCP adverse events in children, pooled post-ERCP pancreatitis (PEP) incidence when study-level data allowed, and summarized reported risk factors and prevention strategies.
elements.reason: The need for the review is implied by the stated aim to update evidence and provide a current benchmark ('The pooled estimate provides a current benchmark'), but the importance and need for conducting the review are not explicitly argued in a dedicated rationale statement in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: We updated the evidence on post-ERCP adverse events in children... Prior systematic reviews and meta-analyses were used for background comparison and reference checking only.
elements.reason: The manuscript indicates it is an update and that prior systematic reviews exist and were used for benchmarking, but the retrieved evidence does not identify or cite a specific previous systematic review to justify the need for the current update.
This is a review of adverse-event incidence (prognostic/descriptive), not a review of intervention effects; no intervention whose mechanism of action needs describing is evaluated.
This is not a review of complex interventions; no logic model is required, and none is reported in the retrieved evidence.

The retrieved evidence contains no explicit statement of the review objective(s) or question(s), nor any question-formulation framework. The title implies objectives, but no explicit objectives statement appears in any retrieved chunk.
This is a review of intervention effects (PEP incidence, risk factors, prevention strategies), but no planned comparisons stated using PICO or a variant are present in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Inclusion Criteria: Study Type: Original pediatric studies, including cohort studies, case-control studies, and randomized or nonrandomized interventional studies... Population: Pediatric patients (<18 years) undergoing ERCP. Outcomes: Reported incidence, types, risk factors, or management strategies of post-ERCP complications.
elements.reason: Eligible study designs, population, and outcome requirements are explicitly specified in the inclusion/exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: Language: English. Publication Date: January 1, 2015 to June 26, 2025.
elements.reason: Language and dissemination date range are specified, but no publication or report status restriction (e.g., peer-reviewed vs grey literature) is stated.

elements.quote: Data Availability: Incomplete or unextractable data.
elements.reason: Exclusion for data availability is mentioned, but the review does not distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: We prespecified subgroup exploration by age group, ERCP indication, procedure type, pancreatic duct manipulation or contrast injection, sphincterotomy, and operator or center volume.
elements.reason: Synthesis groups (subgroups, denominator-unit categories, PEP vs other outcomes) are described, but they are not explicitly linked to comparisons defined in the review objectives.

elements.quote: The search was limited to studies published between January 1, 2015, and June 26, 2025, to capture contemporary pediatric ERCP practice, including changes in therapeutic indications, endoscopic accessories, anesthesia support, and prophylaxis strategies.
elements.reason: A rationale is provided for the notable date restriction on eligibility.

elements.quote: The search was limited to studies published between January 1, 2015, and June 26, 2025
elements.reason: Only publication date restrictions are reported; no date on which each database, register, or other source was last searched or consulted is given anywhere in the evidence.

elements.quote: Two reviewers independently searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library
elements.reason: Database names are reported, but no search interface/platform or coverage dates of the databases are specified.

elements.quote: Records from registers & other sources (n = 46) ClinicalTrials.gov (n = 19) WHO ICTRP (n = 13) Reference lists & grey literature (n = 14)

No individuals were reported as contacted to identify studies.

No backward or forward citation searching with a citation index/platform and search date is reported; prior reviews were used only for contextual comparison, not formal citation searching.
No journals or conference proceedings were consulted directly; conference abstracts were explicitly excluded.

elements.quote: The search strategy combined Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) terms and free-text keywords using Boolean operators (AND, OR). Keywords included: 'children', 'pediatric', 'ERCP', 'endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography', 'complications', 'adverse event', 'pancreatitis', 'bleeding', 'perforation', and 'infection'.
elements.reason: Keywords and Boolean approach are reported for four databases, but the full database-specific search strings as actually run (exact MeSH terms, syntax per database) are not provided, and no supplementary search strategy file is referenced.

elements.quote: The search was limited to studies published between January 1, 2015, and June 26, 2025, to capture contemporary pediatric ERCP practice, including changes in therapeutic indications, endoscopic accessories, anesthesia support, and prophylaxis strategies.
elements.reason: Date and language limits are stated and the date limit is justified by reference to contemporary practice; language limit (English) is listed in eligibility criteria.
No published search filters or adaptations are cited anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No evidence that natural-language processing or text-analysis tools were used to identify or refine search terms.

elements.reason: Independent work by two reviewers during study selection is explicitly reported.

elements.quote: Any discrepancies in study selection were resolved through discussion or consultation with a third reviewer.

elements.quote: Data extraction was independently conducted by two reviewers using a standardized form.

elements.reason: Disagreement resolution process (discussion or third reviewer) is described.

elements.reason: Decision rules for handling denominator units and multiple reporting formats are described, but rules for selecting among multiple reports of the same study are not explicitly stated.

elements.quote: we collected first author, year, country, study design, sample size, number of ERCP procedures, mean or median age, ERCP indications, procedure type, follow-up duration, adverse-event definitions or reporting windows, event numerators and denominators for PEP, bleeding, perforation, cholangitis or infection, severity classification, risk factors, and management strategies
elements.reason: Outcomes (PEP, bleeding, perforation, cholangitis/infection, severity, risk factors, management) are listed and extraction of adverse-event definitions/reporting windows is described, but formal definitions of each outcome domain are not fully provided.

elements.quote: adverse-event definitions or reporting windows

elements.reason: The manuscript implies selection of extractable results (e.g., only studies with extractable numerators/denominators pooled; risk factors summarized narratively when not poolable), but it does not explicitly state whether all compatible results within each outcome domain were sought.

elements.quote: Formal subgroup meta-analysis was not forced when studies did not provide stratified PEP event counts... These variables were therefore summarized as explanatory domains for heterogeneity and risk.
elements.reason: Some selection processes are described (pooling only outcomes with ≥3 studies with extractable data; narrative synthesis otherwise), but a general method for deciding which results to collect within each outcome domain is not fully articulated.

elements.quote: In response to peer review, we also added a post hoc denominator-unit sensitivity summary, separating procedure-level studies from patient-level or first-ERCP-perchild studies
elements.reason: A post hoc analysis change is reported with rationale (peer review), but this concerns analysis strategy rather than outcome-domain inclusion or definitions; no changes to outcome definitions are reported.

elements.quote: Random-effects pooling was performed for PEP because this outcome had the most consistently extractable numerators and denominators. Bleeding, perforation, and cholangitis were less frequent and were summarized descriptively
elements.reason: PEP is identified as the primary/most important outcome with rationale (most consistently extractable data; most frequent and clinically significant complication), while other outcomes were summarized descriptively.

elements.quote: For each primary study, we collected first author, year, country, study design, sample size, number of ERCP procedures, mean or median age, ERCP indications, procedure type, follow-up duration, adverse-event definitions or reporting windows, event numerators and denominators for PEP, bleeding, perforation, cholangitis or infection, severity classification, risk factors, and management strategies.
elements.reason: The Data Extraction section explicitly lists all variables sought, including participant, procedural, outcome, and risk-factor characteristics.

We retained the denominator unit used by the source rather than converting procedure-level data to patient-level data when repeat procedures per child were not consistently reported.
elements.reason: The authors describe assumptions made about unclear information, specifically how unclear or mixed denominator units were handled rather than converted.

No tool or framework used to determine which data items to collect is cited anywhere in the retrieved evidence; only a 'standardized form' is mentioned without citation or reference to a guiding tool.

elements.quote: Non-randomized primary studies were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), randomized trials using RoB 2, and prior systematic reviews or meta-analyses using AMSTAR 2[16-18].
elements.reason: Three named risk-of-bias tools are specified and matched to study designs.

elements.quote: Rather than reproducing checklist content, we summarized each study's overall judgment and used these judgments to grade confidence across evidence domains.
elements.reason: The domains or items assessed by each tool (NOS, RoB 2, AMSTAR 2) are not described; the authors explicitly state they did not reproduce checklist content.

elements.quote: Rather than reproducing checklist content, we summarized each study's overall judgment and used these judgments to grade confidence across evidence domains.
elements.reason: An overall judgment was made and used, but the rules for deriving the overall judgment are not reported.

elements.quote: Non-randomized primary studies were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), randomized trials using RoB 2, and prior systematic reviews or meta-analyses using AMSTAR 2[16-18].
elements.reason: Standard tools were used as named; no adaptations are reported or implied.

elements.quote: Non-randomized primary studies were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), randomized trials using RoB 2, and prior systematic reviews or meta-analyses using AMSTAR 2[16-18].
elements.reason: Only existing tools were used; no new tool was developed.

elements.quote: The methodological quality and risk of bias of each eligible source were independently assessed by two reviewers using tools appropriate to study design. Disagreements were resolved by consensus, with a third reviewer consulted when needed.
elements.reason: Two independent reviewers, with consensus and third-reviewer resolution of disagreements, are reported.

elements.quote: The methodological quality and risk of bias of each eligible source were independently assessed by two reviewers using tools appropriate to study design.
elements.reason: No evidence of contacting study investigators for risk-of-bias information; the process described does not indicate such contact was attempted or needed.

elements.quote: AI-assisted tools were used during revision for language editing and formatting checks.
elements.reason: No automation tools were used for risk-of-bias assessment; AI tools were used only for language editing.

elements.quote: Results were expressed as pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
elements.reason: The statistical analysis section specifies the effect measures: pooled proportions with 95% CIs for incidence outcomes (random-effects models for proportions), and reported odds ratios with 95% CIs for risk factors displayed descriptively (text_30, Figure 5 caption: 'Reported odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals are shown').

elements.quote: Heterogeneity was interpreted as low, moderate, substantial, or considerable using conventional thresholds
elements.reason: While heterogeneity interpretation thresholds are referenced as 'conventional', no explicit numeric thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect sizes (e.g., what constitutes a clinically important OR or proportion) and their rationale are reported.

elements.quote: Random-effects meta-analysis of logittransformed proportions across 15 non-overlapping primary studies
elements.reason: Re-expression via logit transformation of proportions is described (also 'transformed values, standard errors' in Additional file 5), but no explicit methods for re-expressing synthesized results into another effect measure (e.g., converting proportions to risk ratios) are described.

elements.quote: Pooled incidences were estimated using random-effects models for proportions, with variance stabilization for rare events where appropriate.
elements.reason: A partial rationale is given (variance stabilization for rare events; random-effects due to heterogeneity), and the decision not to pool risk-factor estimates is justified by differing exposure definitions, but no explicit justification for choosing proportions/logit transformation as the effect measure is provided.

elements.quote: Meta-analysis was conducted only for outcomes reported by at least three non-overlapping primary studies with extractable numerators and denominators. ... Formal subgroup meta-analysis was not forced when studies did not provide stratified PEP event counts ... Risk-factor effect estimates were not pooled when exposure definitions, covariate adjustment, or reporting units differed substantially. These data were summarized narratively
elements.reason: The Statistical Analysis section explicitly describes the criteria and processes deciding which studies entered each synthesis (quantitative meta-analysis vs narrative synthesis), including minimum study count, extractability, non-overlap, and denominator-unit handling; the abstract (text_2) and text_11 corroborate the separation of primary studies from prior reviews to avoid double counting.

elements.quote: For PEP, we recorded whether the denominator represented ERCP procedures, patients, first ERCP per child, or a mixed/unclear reporting unit. We retained the denominator unit used by the source rather than converting procedure-level data to patient-level data when repeat procedures per child were not consistently reported.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes data preparation methods: recording and retaining denominator units rather than converting, plus statistical analysis methods (logit transformation, variance stabilization for rare events, denominator-unit sensitivity categories) covering data conversions and handling of non-extractable/missing statistics.

elements.quote: Table 1 now reports the study-level numerator, denominator, percentage, denominator unit, and available definition or reporting note for every study contributing to the PEP synthesis.
elements.reason: Tabular structures (Table 1 with study-level PEP data; Table 2 risk factors; Table 4 comparison) and their contents are described, but this description appears in Results/Additional Files rather than as an explicit Methods account of tabulation approaches.

elements.quote: Figure 2. Forest plot of PEP incidence after pediatric ERCP. Random-effects meta-analysis of logittransformed proportions across 15 non-overlapping primary studies... Figure 8. Funnel plot for PEP incidence after pediatric ERCP. Exploratory funnel plot based on logittransformed PEP proportions...
elements.reason: Graphical displays (forest plot, funnel plot, evidence map, bar graphs, effect-estimate plot) are described in figure captions and Results, and the Methods mention 'displayed as reported estimates' and funnel plots, but a consolidated Methods description of graphical methods is absent.
No basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or graphs (e.g., alphabetical, chronological, by weight) is reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Because covariate adjustment varied across source studies, this visual summary is descriptive rather than a pooled predictor meta-analysis.
elements.reason: Rationale is provided for some non-standard displays (e.g., Figure 5 as descriptive rather than pooled; Figure 4 'hypothesis-generating rather than definitive'; funnel plot 'exploratory'), but not systematically for all non-standard figures (e.g., evidence map, prevention bar chart, framework figure).
No statistical software package or version is reported anywhere; only a PowerShell script for figure generation is mentioned (text_30), which is not statistical synthesis software.

elements.quote: Risk-factor effect estimates were not pooled when exposure definitions, covariate adjustment, or reporting units differed substantially. These data were summarized narratively and, where appropriate, displayed as reported estimates.
elements.reason: Alternative narrative synthesis is described and justified when pooling was not possible.

elements.quote: Pooled incidences were estimated using random-effects models for proportions, with variance stabilization for rare events where appropriate.
elements.reason: The random-effects model for proportions is reported, with rationale tied to rare-event handling.

elements.quote: Pooled incidences were estimated using random-effects models for proportions, with variance stabilization for rare events where appropriate.
elements.reason: The statistical method (random-effects pooling of proportions with variance stabilization) is described; logit transformation is confirmed in Figure 2 caption.

elements.quote: Between-study heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran Q and the I-squared statistic.
elements.reason: Heterogeneity assessment methods (Cochran Q, I-squared, and tau-squared) are explicitly reported.
Tau-squared is reported as a result (0.412) but the between-study variance estimator (e.g., DerSimonian-Laird, REML) is never specified.
Confidence intervals are reported as results but the method for calculating summary-effect CIs is not described.

elements.quote: with variance stabilization for rare events where appropriate
elements.reason: Some implementation detail (variance stabilization for rare events) is given, but the specific transformation/estimator details are not fully specified.

elements.quote: Pooled incidences were estimated using random-effects models for proportions
elements.reason: A frequentist (non-Bayesian) meta-analysis was performed, so prior distributions do not apply.

elements.quote: Meta-analysis was conducted only for outcomes reported by at least three non-overlapping primary studies with extractable numerators and denominators.
elements.reason: Statistical dependency is handled by restricting the meta-analysis to non-overlapping primary studies.

elements.quote: Formal subgroup meta-analysis was not forced when studies did not provide stratified PEP event counts, because doing so would have required ecological assumptions.
elements.reason: Planned syntheses judged inappropriate (subgroup and risk-factor pooling) are identified with explicit reasons.

elements.quote: We prespecified subgroup exploration by age group, ERCP indication, procedure type, pancreatic duct manipulation or contrast injection, sphincterotomy, and operator or center volume.
elements.reason: Methods for exploring heterogeneity (subgroup exploration by prespecified factors) are explicitly described in the Statistical Analysis section.

elements.quote: We prespecified subgroup exploration by age group, ERCP indication, procedure type, pancreatic duct manipulation or contrast injection, sphincterotomy, and operator or center volume.
elements.reason: Factors are named, but specific factor levels and expected direction of effect modification are not reported; formal subgroup meta-analysis was not performed when stratified counts were unavailable.

elements.quote: Formal subgroup meta-analysis was not forced when studies did not provide stratified PEP event counts, because doing so would have required ecological assumptions. These variables were therefore summarized as explanatory domains for heterogeneity and risk.
elements.reason: The manuscript implies study-level (ecological) analysis was avoided and variables were summarized narratively, but it does not explicitly state whether analyses used study-level variables, within-study contrasts, or both.
No methods for formally comparing subgroup effects (e.g., interaction tests, Q-test between subgroups) are reported; formal subgroup meta-analysis was explicitly not performed.

elements.quote: These variables were therefore summarized as explanatory domains for heterogeneity and risk. ... These data were summarized narratively and, where appropriate, displayed as reported estimates.
elements.reason: Informal/narrative exploration of heterogeneity is described, including the prespecified factors (age group, indication, procedure type, duct manipulation, sphincterotomy, operator/center volume) used as explanatory domains.

elements.quote: In response to peer review, we also added a post hoc denominator-unit sensitivity summary, separating procedure-level studies from patient-level or first-ERCP-perchild studies and retaining a mixed/unclear category when the source did not permit classification.
